returnInterest.note: Definitely wants to come back as soon as possible.

description.intro: The Philippines stood out for its amazing food, beautiful seas, nature, and relaxing atmosphere, especially outside the major cities in the province.
tips: Visit the province outside the big cities for the best beaches, scenery, and atmosphere.
thingsToKnow: Smaller islands can experience temporary power outages during the day.
culturalNotes: Indoor spaces are often kept very cool with strong ventilation and cooling.
personalNotes: Loved trying pork lechon, adobo, and pork sisig.
Enjoyed boat rides and relaxing by the sea while looking at distant islands.
Personally really enjoyed the atmosphere in the Philippines.
Thought the experience felt absolutely amazing.

travelPracticalities.visaNotes: Did not need a visa for entry, but needed to complete an Electronic Travel Declaration within 72 hours before the flight using https://etravel.gov.ph/. After arrival and scanning the declaration, I was allowed to stay up to 30 days visa-free.
travelPracticalities.currencyNotes: The local currency is the Philippine Peso (PHP). Cash is the primary payment method; especially in the province, but cards are commonly accepted in cities.
transportTips: Taxis near locations such as: airports, big malls, and boat ports usually charge higher prices; especially for foreigners
Ferries may depart on time but often arrive later than estimated.
Bangka (bangca) boats are commonly used by locals for island transport.
Due to heavy traffic in large cities, cars and taxis can be quite slow.
languageTips: The two official languages are Tagalog and English.
People usually speak perfect/very good English.
Some people in the province may not be able to speak English.
The Philippines has many languages and dialects.
Tagalog is mainly spoken in the north near Manila.
Bisaya (Cebuano) is commonly spoken in the central Philippines near Cebu.

seasonalNotes.notes: Very hot and sunny weather, but very bearable near coastal island areas.
